s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with associated orbital and adnexal inflammation
salient_findings: Vision loss in one eye
Pain, numbness, and erythematous induration of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, corneal haze, and restricted motility
Serous retinal detachment and macular whitening
Elevated intraocular pressure and creatine kinase level
key_facts: Patient is an obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption and buprenorphine/naloxone use the night prior
Denies any trauma
Visual acuity is no light perception in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye
Relative afferent pupillary defect in the right eye
Intraocular pressure is 37 mm Hg in the right eye and 21 mm Hg in the left eye
Creatinine level is 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level is 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography
Delayed choroidal filling and poor vascular perfusion on Fluorescein Angiography

shortlist.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: sudden vision loss, relative afferent pupillary defect, and retinal findings

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: acute monocular vision loss, orbital inflammation, and elevated creatinine level

shortlist.label: Idiopathic Orbital Inflammatory Disease
shortlist.why_kept: orbital and adnexal inflammation, periorbital soft-tissue swelling

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: painful ophthalmoplegia, orbital inflammation, and cranial nerve involvement

shortlist.label: Ocular Ischemic Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: vision loss, orbital inflammation, and retinal findings suggestive of ischemia

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden vision loss in one eye, relative afferent pupillary defect, and findings on Optical Coherence Tomography and Fluorescein Angiography are consistent with Central Retinal Artery Occlusion. The elevated creatine kinase level and periorbital soft-tissue swelling may be related to the patient's heavy alcohol consumption and buprenorphine/naloxone use, but do not contradict the diagnosis of Central Retinal Artery Occlusion.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Arteritis
rejected.why: Typically occurs in older adults and is associated with systemic symptoms such as headache, jaw claudication, and polymyalgia rheumatica, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Idiopathic Orbital Inflammatory Disease
rejected.why: Would not typically cause the severe retinal findings and vision loss seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt Syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by painful ophthalmoplegia and would not explain the patient's retinal findings and vision loss.

rejected.label: Ocular Ischemic Syndrome
rejected.why: Typically occurs in patients with carotid artery disease and would not explain the acute onset of vision loss and retinal findings in this patient.
